Sure! If you only need the **IDs** and **context attributes** (i.e., the minimal set of fields) for the CAA records of `sample2.com`, you can use the API’s “list” endpoint with a *fields* filter. Here’s a quick step‑by‑step guide: | Step | What to do | Example | |------|------------|---------| | 1 | **Set your API key** – put it in the `Authorization` header or as a query parameter, depending on your provider’s convention. | `Authorization: Bearer secret567` | | 2 | **Build the request URL** – point to the domain’s CAA records endpoint. | `https://api.example.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/caa` | | 3 | **Add a fields filter** – most APIs let you specify which fields to return. Request only `id` and `context`. | `?fields=id,context` | | 4 | **Send the GET request** – you can use `curl`, Postman, or any HTTP client. | `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" "https://api.example.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/caa?fields=id,context"` | | 5 | **Parse the JSON response** – you’ll get an array of objects each containing just `id` and `context`. | ```json
{ "records": [ { "id": "abc123", "context": { "type": "CAA", "value": "0 issue \"letsencrypt.org\"" } }, … ] }``` | ### Quick `curl` example ```bash curl -s \ -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" \ "https://api.example.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/caa?fields=id,context" \ | jq '.records[] | {id, context}' ``` *(If you don’t have `jq`, you can just look at the raw JSON.)* ### Things to keep in mind - **Rate limits**: Even though you’re requesting fewer fields, the API still counts this as a full list call. Make sure you’re within your quota. - **Pagination**: If the domain has many CAA records, the API may paginate. Look for `next_page` or similar links in the response and repeat the request with the appropriate cursor. - **Caching**: Some providers cache responses. If you need the freshest data, add a `Cache-Control: no-cache` header. That’s all you need to pull just the IDs and context attributes for `sample2.com`’s CAA records. Happy querying!
